title: Microsoft rolls out Autopilot and unified Copilot app at Ignite 2026
subtitle: The new long-running agent gets its own Entra identity and @-mentions in Teams; Foundry extends to AKS and Word, Excel and PowerPoint now live inside the Copilot app.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Microsoft used Ignite 2026, held November 17–20 in San Francisco, to launch Autopilot — a long-running personal agent with its own Entra identity and persistent memory that colleagues can @-mention in Teams. Autopilot is rolling out to Frontier early-access customers first, not generally available; pricing was not disclosed in the keynote. In parallel, Microsoft made Copilot Home generally available, introduced Copilot Workspaces, and promoted Copilot Managed Runtime to GA. Word, Excel and PowerPoint now run inside the Copilot app. Foundry's continuous-improvement loop — multi-turn evaluation, insights and Agent Optimizer — reached GA, with human annotation and managed training in preview, and Foundry is extending to Azure Kubernetes Service in preview so open-weight models and agents can move from experimentation into production clusters.

The identity choice is the newsworthy design decision. By giving Autopilot its own Entra ID, Microsoft treats the agent as a distinct principal in the access-control graph — actions it takes are tied to that agent ID, surfaced to admins, and auditable the way a service account would be. That is the opposite of the pattern where an agent impersonates its user. The practical consequence: when Autopilot pushes to a repo or emails a vendor, the trail is the agent's, and an admin can revoke its scope without breaking the user's credentials. This is the same architectural choice Anthropic made with Claude's per-tool authentication, now extended to a persistent personal agent.

Ignite also previewed where Microsoft is competing. Autopilot plus the unified Copilot app is the response to Anthropic's Claude Duet and OpenAI's Dots — persistent agents that live beside the user rather than inside a chat tab. Foundry on AKS is the answer to AWS Bedrock AgentCore and Google Agent Development Kit. Microsoft's coding model family is now in GitHub Copilot and Foundry, with a flagship and a cheaper Flash variant. The platform story is converging: every hyperscaler is shipping a long-running agent with its own identity, its own memory, and its own compliance surface — which means the differentiator over the next year will be governance tools, not the agent itself.

A note for learners: watch how companies grant and revoke agent identities over the next 12 months. The interesting work is not in model prompting but in the surrounding plumbing — how an agent gets scoped access to a vendor portal, how its actions are logged, how a user offboards it when they leave. If you are early-career and want to build defensible skills, learn the IAM, OIDC, and audit-logging side of agent deployment. The models get commoditized faster than the governance does.
